activity.title: We just shipped Dream at Mem0 . Most agents today write memory but nothing ever cleans it up. So you end up with the same fact stored five different ways, old preferences that stopped being true months ago, and related details sitting in separate memories that never talk to each other. We saw this in our own data. A typical active project was carrying a few hundred memories quietly duplicating or contradicting each other. Dream runs in the background and fixes that. It merges the repeats, supersedes the stale facts while keeping the old one as history, and builds patterns out of many memories instead of leaving them scattered. The pattern part is the one I find most interesting. A support agent can start seeing the recurring issue across hundreds of tickets instead of treating every ticket as new. A therapy use case can pick up behavioral patterns in a patient over months. If problems like this sound fun to you, we are hiring: https://mem0.ai/careers ...more

We just shipped an updated version of Mem0’s Token-Efficient Memory Algorithm with Temporal Reasoning. In April, we launched the first version of the algorithm and called out multi-session reasoning and temporal reasoning as two of the hardest categories in memory. This release improves both at top_200: - Temporal reasoning: +3.8 pts - Multi-session reasoning: +1.5 pts The updated algorithm now reaches 92.5 on LoCoMo and 94.4 on LongMemEval, while keeping retrieval under <7,000 tokens per call. The April version was built around single-pass extraction and hierarchical retrieval. This update adds two more capabilities: Temporal Reasoning gives every memory a time signature, so agents can understand when something happened, whether it is still active, and what kind of memory it is. Memory Decay adds recency-aware ranking, so stale memories remain available without dominating current queries. This matters because long-running agents do not just need more memory. They need memory that can tell what changed, what is still true, and what should no longer be treated as current. Same API. No migration needed. Live on Mem0 platform today. AI was supposed to flatten the gap between engineers. Imo it's done the opposite. Vibe coding an MVP is basically solved - anyone can ship a working app in a weekend, that part's real. But 2 weeks in, when your service is dying under real load or you're chasing some weird concurrency bug, AI can't reason about your system for you. That's still on you. And that's exactly where you can tell who has CS fundamentals and who's been faking it. Shaky fundamentals + AI maybe gets you to 5x. Solid fundamentals, you can hit 1000x. The gap got bigger, not smaller.

From my experience building Mem0 with Taranjeet Singh , I’ve seen why filesystem memory does not hold up in production. It can work for demos, prototypes, and small personal agents. But production changes the equation: → Cost: Loading 100K tokens of memory per query at $3/million input tokens adds up fast. At 10,000 queries/day, that's $3/day just for memory tokens, or roughly $90/month. Selective retrieval at 2K tokens per query cuts that to $1.80/month. The difference compounds with scale. → Latency: More input tokens means slower time-to-first-token → Dataset Grows: Current benchmarks use a fixed conversation. Production memory grows continuously. The filesystem approach that works at 50K tokens breaks at 500K. Filesystem memory optimizes for a snapshot. A dedicated memory system optimizes for a trajectory that evolves over time. As agents become long-running, multi-user, and production-facing, memory needs to move from files to infrastructure. See below to read more 👇 https://lnkd.in/gfs34Px4 ...more

Human memory needs sleep to make sense of the day. It replays what happened, strengthens what matters, connects it to what you already know, and lets the rest fade. AI agents never got that part. They write memory constantly, but nothing organizes it. Facts get restated in different words. Old info stays active long after it's stopped being true. Related details stay scattered across memories that never get connected. We looked at our own data. The typical active mem0 project was carrying a few hundred memories that quietly duplicated or contradicted each other. So we built Dream. It's a background process that does for an agent's memory what sleep does for us. It runs three things: - Merge: facts that repeat get folded into one clear memory - Supersede: the old fact stays as history, the new fact becomes the truth - Synthesis: not one memory, but a pattern built from many, traced back to every source it came from Try it now: https://lnkd.in/gPjVAmri Live today on Pro and Enterprise.
